exact_claim: Solo operators with client-facing AI work currently experience unmet pain around proving what their AI did, such that a cryptographic receipt + replay surface would meaningfully change their behavior.
what_would_confirm: At least 7 of 12 A3 interviewees spontaneously describe a specific incident in the last 90 days where they could not prove, reconstruct, or defend an AI output when a client/collaborator asked.
what_would_falsify: Fewer than 3 of 12 A3 interviewees report any incident of AI-output-proof pain; most say screenshots or copy-paste logs are sufficient.
fastest_test: A3 interview question: 'Has anyone asked you to prove what an AI did for you? Tell me about that.'
notes: The keystone wedge hypothesis. If this falsifies, the entire wedge is wrong — not just a framing issue.

exact_claim: A3 (AI-native creator/consultant) segment has higher urgency around receipted AI work than A1 (solo sovereign builder), because A3 has external accountability to clients while A1 has only internal accountability.
what_would_confirm: A3 interviewees articulate receipt-need more concretely than A1 (e.g., name specific client moments). A1 articulates receipts as 'nice to have' or ideology-driven; A3 articulates as response to external pressure.
what_would_falsify: A3 and A1 articulate equal urgency, OR A1 articulates higher urgency (would mean wedge is ideology-driven, not mission-driven, which would shift the primary segment).
fastest_test: Compare first unprompted pain mentions between A3 and A1 interview cohorts.
notes: Tests whether to hold A3 primary or swap to A1 primary.

exact_claim: Users facing the pain in H1 will reshape their workflow around a tool that produces portable signed receipts, not merely treat receipts as a nice addition.
what_would_confirm: At least 3 interviewees describe what they would stop doing (e.g., stop screenshotting, stop maintaining ad-hoc logs) if receipts existed.
what_would_falsify: Interviewees say 'interesting' but cannot name anything they would stop or change; receipt is additive, not replacive.
fastest_test: 'What would you stop doing if you had this?' close-out question.
notes: If falsified, wedge may still be real but monetization path weakens — receipts become vitamin, not painkiller.

exact_claim: A portable, signed, chain-linked record is what users mean when they say they want 'proof' of an AI output, as opposed to vendor-logo timestamps or transcript snapshots.
what_would_confirm: When shown a mock signed-record artifact vs a screenshot + timestamp, interviewees prefer the signed-record AND can articulate why (tamper-evidence, independent verification).
what_would_falsify: Interviewees see no meaningful difference, OR prefer the screenshot because it is readable.
fastest_test: Mock artifact comparison in interview (side-by-side image).
notes: Risk: users may want social proof rather than cryptographic proof. GUARDRAIL 3: external wording defaults to 'signed record / verifiable record / proof of what the AI did'; 'cryptographic receipt' is internal terminology only. Naming validation itself is H13.

exact_claim: Target users prefer local-first AI execution for mission-level (i.e., important, high-trust) work, even when this costs UX convenience.
what_would_confirm: At least 5 of 12 interviewees already run some AI workload locally (Ollama, LM Studio, local Whisper, etc.). Expressed preference for data-retention under their control during mission-level work.
what_would_falsify: Most interviewees use exclusively cloud AI and cannot articulate any discomfort with that pattern.
fastest_test: Screening question + follow-up: 'What fraction of your AI use is cloud vs local?' + 'When would you choose local?'
notes: Partially validated externally via Signal/ProtonMail analog (ranked SIGNAL in audit Phase 2); needs direct corroboration on AI specifically.

exact_claim: A single CLI face (Dema) is acceptable — not a blocker — for the primary and secondary segments in 2026.
what_would_confirm: At least 8 of 12 A3/A1 interviewees say they install and use CLI tools weekly OR have installed at least 3 dev-tool CLIs this year (gh, jq, ripgrep etc.).
what_would_falsify: Most interviewees avoid CLI tools OR describe CLI as hostile; only use web/GUI AI tools.
fastest_test: Screening question: 'When you need to try a dev tool
missions_affected: what format do you use?' + observe behavior ('show me your terminal').
column11: If weak, shift wedge timing to wait for browser-face (Row 6 trust surface complete + GUI build); extends timeline by 2-3 months.

exact_claim: Users who feel H1-H3 pain will pay a non-zero amount for an external verifier-as-a-service or a paid receipt-archive tier, once the free local binary is in use.
what_would_confirm: 3+ interviewees name a price range when asked about verifier-as-a-service AND at least 1 says they would pay within 60 days of first use.
what_would_falsify: 0 interviewees name a positive price, OR all say 'only if free'.
fastest_test: WTP probe: 'If a shareable public verifier URL existed for these receipts
missions_affected: what would that be worth to you monthly?'
column11: Business-model fallback: if WTP is zero, the wedge can still ship (adoption engine) but monetization requires rethinking — possibly enterprise-later path.

exact_claim: Receipts will be shared externally by operators with clients/collaborators/peers at a rate that becomes a visible marketing channel.
what_would_confirm: 3+ interviewees spontaneously describe a scenario where they would send a receipt externally — AND can name at least one recipient by role (e.g., 'I would send this to my client project manager').
what_would_falsify: 0 interviewees describe sharing; or they describe sharing only summary language, not the receipt artifact.
fastest_test: Scenario probe: 'Walk me through who you would send this to
column11: The viral-loop assumption. If falsified, adoption depends on outbound marketing, which is expensive for a solo-founder stage.

exact_claim: A significant fraction of target users have concrete pain from frontier-model vendor dependency (quota, pricing, deprecation, lock-in) — strong enough that model-portability anchors their tool evaluation.
what_would_confirm: At least 4 of 12 interviewees describe a specific vendor-dependency incident (rate-limited during deadline, price-shock email, model deprecation mid-project).
what_would_falsify: Most interviewees describe their cloud AI as stable and sufficient; dependency is not on their radar.
fastest_test: 'Tell me about the last time a cloud AI tool let you down mid-task.'
notes: A8 (stretch segment) directly tests this. Broader corroboration from GPU-cost inflation signal (audit P1).

exact_claim: Replay is valued specifically — not as a vague 'reproducibility' notion but as 'run the same mission again on the same inputs and get the same output bound to the original receipt'.
what_would_confirm: When explained, 3+ interviewees articulate a concrete scenario where replay would help them (debugging, audit defense, client challenge).
what_would_falsify: Interviewees confuse replay with 'ask the AI the same question again' OR see no value difference.
fastest_test: Explain replay concretely → ask for a use-case in their work.
notes: Isolates whether row 4's PROVEN value translates into user-visible demand, or is just engineering elegance.

exact_claim: Users will not use a mission-centric tool unless the mission lifecycle (states traversed, chosen model, gates passed) is visible — the receipt alone is not enough.
what_would_confirm: Interviewees respond positively to a receipt showing states_traversed, ihsan_score, chosen_model — and negatively to a receipt that hides it.
what_would_falsify: Interviewees find the lifecycle detail overwhelming or irrelevant; want only input + output.
fastest_test: Mock receipt A (detailed) vs mock receipt B (minimal) preference test.
notes: If falsified, trim the receipt surface for launch; keep the rich version for advanced users.

exact_claim: Founder self-interview is PREP ONLY — used to calibrate wording, surface interviewer bias, and rehearse probes. EXCLUDED from all signal counts, hypothesis confirmation or falsification, sprint interview totals, and proceed/narrow/reframe/kill thresholds.
what_would_confirm: Founder produces a Template-1 interview_type=founder_prep artifact on Day 1 with at least one candidate pain-incident + at least one self-identified interviewer bias to watch for.
what_would_falsify: Founder self-interview is skipped OR its outputs leak into external evidence aggregation.
fastest_test: Founder fills Template 1 with interview_type=founder_prep; QA review ensures no aggregation leak.
notes: GUARDRAIL 1: separated from external evidence per operator instruction 2026-04-23. Prior framing (alone-first doctrine → founder-as-A1 signal) deferred; treat founder voice only as interviewer calibration input. Previous H12 claim about founder-as-valid-A1 withdrawn until external evidence exists.

exact_claim: External wording 'signed record' / 'verifiable record' / 'proof of what the AI did' will outperform 'cryptographic receipt' as launch language for primary segment A3. Naming is itself under test, not a given.
what_would_confirm: Message-test cards leading with 'signed record' language produce at least 2x the named-incident reply rate vs matched cards leading with 'cryptographic receipt' language. Interview wording-preference probe also favors 'signed record'.
what_would_falsify: 'Signed record' and 'cryptographic receipt' produce equivalent response rates OR 'cryptographic receipt' wins.
fastest_test: A/B message-card variant test in the same channel + Q11 wording-preference probe in interviews.
notes: GUARDRAIL 3: crypto-native vocabulary may depress A3 signal. External surfaces default to 'signed record'; 'cryptographic receipt' remains internal/technical documentation only until external evidence supports promoting it.
